title: Former national security adviser John Bolton is indicted by a federal grand
description_short: Former national security adviser John Bolton is indicted by a federal grand jury, and is the third critic of President Trump facing criminal charges in a few weeks
description_medium: NBC News reported that a federal grand jury indicted former national security adviser John Bolton in Maryland on October 16, 2025. The indictment charged eight counts of transmitting national defense information and ten counts of retaining it. The timeline lists October 14, so the event date conflicts with the linked report and needs reconciliation.
description_long: On October 16, 2025, a federal grand jury in Maryland indicted John Bolton, a former national security adviser and prominent Trump critic, according to NBC News. The indictment includes eight counts of transmitting national defense information and ten counts of retaining it. Prosecutors had investigated whether Bolton improperly kept classified material after his acrimonious departure from the first Trump administration. NBC reported that the case followed other criminal cases against prominent Trump adversaries, but that sequence does not establish political motive. At a White House event that day, Trump said he did not know about the indictment and called Bolton “a bad person.” The charges are allegations, not a verdict, and the material provided does not establish Bolton’s guilt. The timeline lists October 14, while NBC reports that the grand jury indicted Bolton on October 16; the discrepancy should be resolved before the event date is finalized.

title: Trump: RFK Jr. announces new dietary guidelines, downplays risks of saturated fat and excessive alcohol consumption
description_short: Trump: RFK Jr. announces new dietary guidelines, downplays risks of saturated fat and excessive alcohol consumption
description_medium: On January 7, 2026, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins, and CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz announced the 2025–2030 U.S. Dietary Guidelines. The supplied account says the guidelines retained a saturated-fat limit while presenting butter and beef tallow favorably, and removed earlier numerical daily alcohol limits. That combination raises questions about how the guidance communicates health risks.
description_long: On January 7, 2026, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins, and CMS Administrator Mehmet Oz announced the 2025–2030 U.S. Dietary Guidelines. The supplied account describes two changes in the guidance: it kept a numerical limit on saturated fat while giving more favorable treatment to butter, beef tallow, and other sources, and it removed the earlier numerical daily limits for alcohol. The combination makes the wording and examples important: a retained limit can sit awkwardly beside positive depictions of foods that contribute to it, while dropping a daily alcohol ceiling does not itself amount to advice that unlimited drinking is safe. The issue is how readers interpret the recommendations and how clearly health risks are communicated. The available account does not establish that the guidelines endorsed unlimited saturated fat or alcohol, or that their announcement changed eating or drinking behavior. It also does not identify the evidence officials used to revise the wording.
